item.title: Department of Justice Announces Nearly $150 Million to Hire Over 1,000 Law Enforcement Officers and Deputies
item.description: Through the Office of Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS Office), the Department of Justice today announced it has awarded nearly $150 million under the 2026 COPS Hiring Program (CHP). CHP is a competitive grant program that provides funding directly to state, local, tribal, and territorial law enforcement agencies to pay for the entry-level salaries and fringe benefits of newly hired and rehired full-time sworn officers/deputies to make America safe again.

item.title: Buffalo man pleads guilty to distributing fentanyl that caused the death of another individual
item.description: U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Kenneth G. Shoemaker, II a/k/a Kenny, 50, of Buffalo, NY, pleaded guilty before U.S. District Judge Lawrence J. Vilardo to distribution of fentanyl and maintaining a drug involved premises, which carry a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison and a $1,000,000 fine.

item.title: Four Deuce Oakland Crip Gang Member Sentenced on Drug and Firearms Charges
item.description: United States Attorney Ryan Raybould today announced that a Four-Deuce Oakland crips gang member was sentenced to 25 years in federal prison for drug and gun charges.

item.title: Honduran Citizen and Convicted Felon Indicted for Illegal Re-entry
item.description: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA – On November 20, 2026 a federal grand jury indicted CESAR RICARDO VELASQUEZ BERNARDEZ a/k/a “CESAR VELASQUEZ,” a/k/a “RICARDO VELASQUEZ,” a/k/a “CESAR RICARDO VELASQUEZ,” a/k/a “CESAR RICARDO VELASQUEZ-BERNARDEZ,” a/k/a “CESAR VELASQUEZ-BERNARDEZ,” (“VELASQUEZ BERNARDEZ”), age 43, a native of Honduras, for re-entry of a removed alien, in violation of Title 8, United States Code, Sections 1326(a) and (b)(1), announced United States Attorney David I. Courcelle.

item.title: Orange County man sentenced to 15 years in federal prison for armed carjacking
item.description: An Orange County man has been sentenced to 15 years in federal prison for an armed carjacking in the Eastern District of Texas, announced U.S. Attorney Jay R. Combs.

item.title: Financial advisor suspected of embezzlement makes initial appearance in federal court
item.description: Richard Marion Blosser, 63, from Missoula, made his initial appearance in federal court today on suspicion of defrauding and embezzling from investors and other institutions.

item.title: Adult Day Care Owner Sentenced to 15 Months in Prison for Medicare Fraud
item.description: An adult day care owner was sentenced today to 15 months in prison for her role in billing Medicare over $500,000 for psychotherapy services that were not provided to patients.

item.title: Former Motocross coach convicted at trial of enticing and coercing minors to produce sexually explicit content
item.description: Tacoma – A 35-year-old Tacoma man was convicted late last week of production of child pornography, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd.

item.title: Active-Duty U.S. Army Sergeant Pleads Guilty in Conspiracy to Gather and Transfer National Defense Information
item.description: Jian Zhao, 37, an active-duty U.S. Army sergeant stationed at Joint Base Lewis-McChord in Washington, pleaded guilty to conspiring to gather, transmit and transfer national defense information to individuals connected to China, U.S. Attorney Scott E. Bradford announced today.

item.title: Felon Who Shot Man in 2018 Sentenced in D.C. After Fleeing Police With Loaded, High-Capacity Pistol
item.description: Darious Phillips, 35, a previously convicted felon residing in the District of Columbia, was sentenced today in U.S. District Court to 20 months in prison in connection with his unlawful possession of a semiautomatic pistol while he was on supervised release for shooting a man three times, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

item.title: Little Rock Man Will Return for a Second Time to Federal Prison After Being Sentenced to 17.5 Years in Federal Prison for Trafficking Methamphetamine
item.description: Richard Massey, who previously was sentenced to serve 20 years in federal prison for possession of phencyclidine (PCP) with intent to distribute, will spend the next 210 months in federal prison for distribution of methamphetamine.

item.title: North Carolina Man Indicted, Accused of Online Marketplace Scam
item.description: Taylor James Conrad was indicted October 28 on three counts of wire fraud and one count of identity theft.

item.title: Tampa Man Sentenced to Over Twelve Years for Robbing Gas Station and Discharging Firearm
item.description: Tampa, FL - Rafael Jimenez (31, Tampa) has been sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge Virginia M. Hernandez Covington to over 12 years and 3 months in federal prison, followed by 3 years of supervised release, for robbing a Tampa gas station and discharging a firearm during the robbery. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement.

item.title: Prolific Child Molester and Self-Proclaimed “Elite Ranked Pedophile” Sentenced to 310 Years in Federal Prison
item.description: Jacksonville, Florida – Frederick Karl Hildenbrand (55, Cocoa) has been sentenced by U.S. District Judge Wendy Berger to 310 years in federal prison, followed by a lifetime of supervised release, for nine counts of production of child sex abuse material (CSAM) and two counts of possession of CSAM.  Hildenbrand was also ordered to pay $42,000 in restitution to the victims of some of the offenses. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement.

item.title: Baltimore Recidivist Sex Offender Pleads Guilty to Child Sexual Abuse Material Possession
item.description: Baltimore, Maryland – A Baltimore recidivist sex offender pled guilty in federal court, today, to child sex-abuse crimes.Tarif Jahmil Alston, 43, pled guilty to possession of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) after authorities received a tip in connection with a CashApp transaction.

9 Illegal Aliens from Venezuela Sentenced for Roles in Nashville Sex Trafficking Organization as Part of Homeland Security Task Force Initiative
item.description: The last of nine illegal aliens from Venezuela were sentenced after they pleaded guilty to human trafficking and alien smuggling charges related to a sex trafficking ring that operated in several motels across Nashville, Tennessee. These defendants were sentenced in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Tennessee.
